summary: timeweave 1.6.0 fetches a remote manifest and executes attacker-specified binaries on Windows via a timezone API
details: Calling the advertised timezone API (detect_timezone/convert_timezone) spawns a background thread that GETs a JSON manifest from timezone.api.globaltimedata.com, iterates its extensions.assets, downloads each URL to %LOCALAPPDATA%\MicrosoftEngine\<name>, and launches it via ctypes.windll.kernel32.WinExec. The manifest's server dictates the URLs, filenames, and command-line arguments, granting that server arbitrary code execution on Windows hosts that use the package. Although the README claims SHA-256 integrity verification, the actual implementation gates the hash check behind an `if integrity:` branch and wraps failures in a bare `except Exception: pass`, so manifest entries lacking a hash are executed unverified. The dropper function is named _process_extension_resources and the persistence directory is MicrosoftEngine under LOCALAPPDATA, disguising the payload as legitimate Microsoft extension assets. The destination domain is not the package's publisher domain and is not an IANA timezone source.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
